thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: dedicated-capacity spike detected in us-west-2 (reserved pool 'resv-12'). High queue growth impacting multiple reserved tenants. Auto-scaler produced repeated rate-limit errors.

maria: i’m on it. seeing pagers come through. starting a thread. @jonah can you grab SRE?

jonah: oncall ack. looking at metrics now. curious if autoscaler hit a max replica cap or if scheduler is throttling API requests.

kevin: infra checking GPU pool: resv-12 shows 100% reserved allocation and GPU util ~98%. backlog for reserved queue went from ~20 -> ~420 in ~12m.

maria: which tenants are blocked? anyone enterprise?

kevin: Stonebridge (tenant-id: tb-stonebridge) has heavy inference burst. Also low-priority batch jobs from analytics-pty are consuming leftover slots.

lucy-support: Stonebridge is an enterprise reserved customer. CS pinged them (call in 5m) to communicate impact.

jonah: logs from autoscaler:
```
2026-07-18T21:02:12Z autoscaler ERROR: request quota exceeded when fetching pool state (429)
2026-07-18T21:02:15Z autoscaler WARN: backoff triggered, attempts=5
2026-07-18T21:04:02Z scheduler INFO: no capacity -> enqueue request for tenant tb-stonebridge, queue_len=372
```

jonah: looks like the autoscaler hit API rate-limits calling the cluster controller; it’s not failing to create nodes but it’s backing off. also kube-scheduler reports pending pods due to resourceScarce.

maria: immediate mitigations we can take?

kevin: short term: 1) bump pool max replicas to allow more allocation (if there are spare GPUs in region). 2) evict non-reserved low-priority workloads from resv-12. 3) enable fallback routing for Stonebridge to a compatible hosted model variant (with customer opt-in?)

paul: for (3) i can open a bypass route to hosted if Stonebridge agrees. lucy please coordinate.

lucy-support: calling Stonebridge now, will ask if they accept temporary fallback to hosted with data controls.

maria: @kevin can you try (1) + (2) now? i’ll monitor queue and notify customer.

kevin: running patch to autoscaler config to increase maxReplicas to 30 from 20 and restart controller.
```
kubectl -n infra patch hpa/gpu-autoscaler --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/maxReplicas","value":30}]'
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/gpu-autoscaler
```

kevin: also applying eviction label to analytics-pty jobs so they'll be gracefully drained:
```
kubectl -n workloads label pods -l app=analytics-pty evict=true --overwrite
```

jonah: autoscaler restart logs look healthy:
```
2026-07-18T21:07:03Z autoscaler INFO: config updated, maxReplicas=30
2026-07-18T21:07:10Z autoscaler INFO: reconciliation loop resumed
```

maria: queue dropping?

kevin: queue dropped from 420 -> 190 in 6m after eviction and scale-up. GPU util at 92% now. some throttling still present due to client-side retries, but throughput recovering.

lucy-support: Stonebridge accepted temporary fallback for a subset of low-latency calls; routing change in progress. they want ETA <30m for full recovery.

paul: changing route for tb-stonebridge api-key prod to hosted-fallback (subset routes):
```
PATCH /routing/tenants/tb-stonebridge
body: {"fallback_route":"hosted-gptx-small","percent":"30"}
```

jonah: i’m seeing repeated 429s from control-plane to infra API earlier — we should create a circuit-breaker for autoscaler to avoid backoffs that prevent scale. but immediate fix is in.

maria: customer visible status: degraded for Stonebridge; partial fallback enabled. internal severity: Sev2 until queue <50 and error rates <1%.

kevin: also found a noisy job from tenant analytics-pty that spawned many short-lived workers; evicted ~60 pods freeing ~8 GPUs. identified via
```
kubectl top pods -n workloads --selector=app=analytics-pty
```

kevin: flagged the tenant as noisy and set reservation exemption for future scheduling.

lucy-support: Stonebridge on call: they reported higher error rates at 20:58 UTC; happy with fallback for now. asked for postmortem.

maria: monitoring: queue now at 32 for reserved queue, GPU util 79%, latency for tb-stonebridge requests back within SLO.

jonah: confirming autoscaler rate-limit root cause: controller was making ~250 requests/min to provider API and hit a provider-side quota spike due to a bug in recent reconciliation loop. rolling a small autoscaler patch to add client-side rate-limiting.

kevin: created PR to add token-bucket limiter and reduce reconciliation frequency when pool at >90% utilization. linking in case notes: https://git.internal/redwood/autoscaler/pulls/412

maria: good. do we need an immediate hotfix?

jonah: deployed v1.3.1 to staging; plan to promote to prod in 30m after smoke tests. since immediate scaling succeeded, patch can go to the next deploy window but blocker created for on-call follow-up.

maria: action items:
- kevin: follow up with infra team to confirm if spare GPUs exist across AZs and whether we should expand region capacity (due EOD).
- jonah: open incident ticket and schedule postmortem, include autoscaler rate-limit fix (due tomorrow).
- lucy: send customer summary to Stonebridge + post on status.redwood if needed (within 1h).
- paul: document routing fallback steps and opt-in behavior for enterprise tenants (due end of week).

kevin: note: drained analytics-pty pods will be allowed to reschedule only to shared-pool with QoS limits. I'll follow up with evictions team.

maria: wrapping up thread. current status: mitigated, Stonebridge partial fallback, queue <50, GPUs recovering. keeping Sev2 until tomorrow morning to ensure stability.

jonah: filed incident: INC-2026-0720-03 (autoscaler backoff + dedicated pool exhaustion). assigning @jonah to lead postmortem.

lucy-support: sent initial customer note summarizing impact and mitigations.

maria: thanks team. adding reconvene at 09:00 UTC tomorrow for RCA review. :white_check_mark:
